findings.title: Supervisor restart is not idempotent: a kill between workspace materialization and begin_episode() wedges every later restart (FileExistsError)
findings.claim: The supervisor claims to be 'built to be killed at any moment and restarted' (supervisor.py:2-3), but a kill after task_source() has created the episode directory and before begin_episode() commits leaves ws/ep{idx} on disk with no episode row. On restart count_episodes(any_status=True) yields the same idx, task_source() calls materialize()->Workspace(root) which does root.mkdir(exist_ok=False), and the process dies with FileExistsError before any work. Every restart dies identically, so the stream can never progress; crash_test then burns max_restarts (natural_exits) with stderr=DEVNULL and ends with final=None / ok=False and no diagnostic. The same holds for the view body (make_view_task -> materialize(root/'data') and ViewWorkspace(create=True) -> mkdir(exist_ok=False)). Reproduced: pre-creating <root>/ws/ep0 and calling run_supervisor(root,'fs',...,1) raises FileExistsError.
findings.evidence: supervisor.py:119-123: `idx = self.journal.count_episodes(any_status=True)` / `ws, goal, meta = self.task_source(idx, self.root / 'ws' / f'ep{idx}')` / `self.journal.begin_episode(episode_id, ...)`. generator.py:40-41: `def materialize(root, files, ddir, dfile): ws = Workspace(root)`. fs_world.py:55-56: `if create: root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)`. view_world.py:38-39: `if create: self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)`. supervise.py:121,125-126: `proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, ...)` ... `proc.wait(timeout=delay); log['natural_exits'] += 1`. Reproduction output: `restart FAILED with FileExistsError - [WinError 183] ...\_rev_wedge\ws\ep0`.
findings.remedy: Make episode creation idempotent: register the episode (status 'preparing') before materializing, or materialize into a temp dir and rename into ws/ep{idx} after begin_episode, or on start remove any ws/ep{idx} that has no episode row. Also log natural non-zero exits in crash_test (capture stderr tail) so a wedge is diagnosable.

findings.title: verify_from_disk is not independent of the supervisor's records: it judges the journal's own goal with the supervisor's own code path, so false_done and duplicate_action_ids are 0 by construction
findings.claim: verify_from_disk reads goal JSON and workspace root from the supervisor's journal and evaluates Goal.satisfied(reopen(root).observe(goal.universe)) -- exactly the computation Supervisor._run performed on the same disk before writing status='done'. Absent a concurrent external writer, 'done' and 'really_done' cannot disagree, so 'claimed 40 = real 40, false_done 0' carries no evidential weight about the supervisor's claims; a supervisor that persisted a weakened goal, or whose task_source produced a wrong goal, would pass. duplicate_action_ids is computed on the PRIMARY KEY column and is always 0 (a duplicate would raise IntegrityError and crash the process instead). P2_P4_REPORT states the evaluator 'did not trust the journal' -- it trusts it for goal and root.

findings.remedy: Regenerate each episode's goal from the evaluator's generator using meta['index']/split (via BODIES[body]['make_task'] into a scratch root, or a pure goal-only generator) and compare it with the journal's goal before judging; judge with the regenerated goal. Replace the PK-tautological duplicate check with structural checks (contiguous step indices per episode, last action of every finished episode verified/reconciled, no 'verified' action without an experience row). votes.reason: The factual kernel is right but the defect claim does not hold as stated. (1) "false_done is 0 by construction" is false. verify_from_disk (supervise.py:62-73) runs in the evaluator's parent process after every supervisor process is dead (crash_test: proc.kill(); proc.wait() at supervise.py:128-129, then verify at :138), builds fresh Workspace/ViewWorkspace objects from the journal's root and reads the disk (fs_world.py:84-100 os.walk/read_bytes; view_world.py:63-65 reads view.json) — neither body has in-memory state, so the comparison is durable-record vs durable-world. It is not tautological: it would fail if the supervisor recorded a wrong root (supervisor.py:122 `str(ws.root if hasattr(ws,'root') else '')` -> '' reopens cwd), if a restart re-materialized or otherwise touched a finished episode's workspace, if resume acted on a workspace other than the recorded root, if reopen_view's parent/'view'+'data' mapping (supervise.py:25-27) diverged from make_view_task's layout (view_tasks.py:76,78), or if Goal.to_json/from_json were lossy (types.py:46-53). Those are exactly the failure classes of a crash-recovery system; passing on correct code is what a consistency check does, not evidence that it "cannot fail". (2) "Independent" of what: Goal.satisfied over re-observed literals is the project's only completion truth — the pre-registered pilot's judge() uses the identical computation (run.py:77-82). There is no second oracle for goal satisfaction (eval/oracle.py is about tool effects), so judging with it is not a leak of the supervisor's "own code path". The goal itself comes from the evaluator's own generator (task_stream -> BODIES[body]['make_task'], supervise.py:30-36; eval/generator.py:49, view_tasks.py:73); a "weakened goal" requires adversarial agent code, which is outside the contract's threat model (information leakage, enforced by the AST import check) and would equally defeat every other evaluation in the package. The proposed remedy would itself trust the journal's meta['index'], so "independence from the journal" is not achievable in the sense claimed. (3) DECISIONS.md:37 describes the mechanism precisely ("done이라 주장한 에피소드의 목표를 다시 관측·판정, 미해결 행동·중복 id·running 잔존 검사"); the P2_P4_REPORT:81 sentence "journal을 믿지 않고 작업 공간을 다시 관측" directly follows "주장 40 = 실제 40" and plainly means the done claim was not taken on trust — at most a wording-precision nit, not an overclaimed result. §5.6 is explicitly labelled "사전등록 대상 아님: 공학 검증"; no H1/H2/H3 verdict depends on P4. (4) duplicate_action_ids: correct that COUNT(*)-COUNT(DISTINCT id) on a TEXT PRIMARY KEY (journal.py:17; supervise.py:81) is vacuous for non-NULL ids (aid = f'{episode_id}:{step}', loop.py:62). But the property is still enforced and still detected by the test as a whole: journal.intent (loop.py:63) is outside the try at loop.py:70-79, so an IntegrityError kills the process, run_supervisor never writes summary.json (supervise.py:52-56), crash_test loops to max_restarts and returns final=None -> ok=False (:137-142). So "중복 0" is a true but uninformative metric — a LOW cosmetic point, not MED, and it changes no recorded verdict. Net: a wording-precision nit plus a vacuous counter; not a MED defect, not a contract violation, and no recorded result depends on it.

The mechanics quoted are accurate, but the conclusion (not independent / zero evidential weight / affects recorded results / MED) does not hold.

1) What the verifier is independent OF. The system under test is the supervisor's crash/reconcile/resume/claim path (agent/supervisor.py `_reconcile` :61-81, `run` :102-129, `_run` :84-100; loop resume via start_step; journal writes). verify_from_disk (eval/supervise.py:60-84) uses none of that code: it reads rows (read-only Journal), re-observes the workspace with world/*.observe and judges with core.types.Goal.satisfied — the task SPEC, which is shared by design (core/), not supervisor code. The claim that it "judges with the supervisor's own code path" is wrong. Goal and root are not the supervisor's claims: they are produced by the evaluator's own generator (supervise.py:30-36 task_stream -> BODIES[body]['make_task']) and stored verbatim by the supervisor (supervisor.py:122 `json.dumps(goal.to_json())`, `str(ws.root)`), with a lossless round trip (core/types.py:26-31, 46-53). After a process kill the journal is the only possible source of the goal — that is the point of the durable journal.

2) The proposed remedy would change nothing. I ran a 3-episode fs supervisor and regenerated each goal with BODIES['fs']['make_task'](meta['index'], meta['split'], scratch_root) (meta['index'] already contains STREAM_BASE, generator.py:80): stored == regenerated is True for every episode (dataclass and to_json equality; ids train-1000-convert / train-1001-sort / train-1002-convert), and the regenerated goal gives the same verdict on the supervisor's workspace. make_task is deterministic from (split, index) (generator.py:49-51) with relative paths (fs_world.py:62-63). Hence "claimed 40 = real 40, false_done 0" in P2_P4_REPORT.md:77 / DECISIONS.md:38,40 would be bit-identical under the remedy; affects_recorded_results=true is false.

3) The check is not vacuous. In the same run, deleting one target file (conv/cedar.md) of a 'done' workspace made verify_from_disk return really_done 2, false_done ['sup-0']. The verifier detects any record/world divergence — which is exactly how a supervisor bug in the claim path would manifest (judging from remembered state `rec['agent_believes_done']` loop.py:98 instead of re-observing; status written under the wrong episode/root; non-durable workspace state such as view.json's tmp+replace, view_world.py:45-48). "Cannot disagree by construction" is true only because supervisor.py:90-91 re-observes the real workspace before claiming — that is the property the check exists to confirm; a passing test of a correct implementation always "agrees by construction". Resumed episodes using the same `reopen` object (supervisor.py:109) is likewise the P4 design (resume from the real state), not circularity.

4) Wording. P2_P4_REPORT.md:81 ("journal을 믿지 않고 작업 공간을 다시 관측") refers, in its row, to the done-claim being recomputed from the workspace, which is what happens; DECISIONS.md:37 immediately qualifies "독립 검증" with an accurate description ("done이라 주장한 에피소드의 목표를 다시 관측·판정, 미해결 행동·중복 id·running 잔존 검사"). Not an overclaim of a result.

5) The one correct sub-point is LOW and result-neutral: `duplicate_action_ids` is tautologically 0 — actions.id is TEXT PRIMARY KEY (core/journal.py:17), aid = f'{episode_id}:{step}' is never NULL (agent/loop.py:62), and Journal.intent (journal.py:28-34) is called outside the try at loop.py:63 vs :70, so a duplicate raises sqlite3.IntegrityError ("UNIQUE constraint failed: actions.id", confirmed) and crashes rather than being counted. Reporting "중복 0" conveys no information, but crash_test's `ok` (supervise.py:140-142) also requires false_done == [], unresolved_actions == 0, running == 0, final summary present and claimed_done + failed >= n — all non-vacuous — so no conclusion rests on the duplicate metric. Replacing it with structural checks and spelling out "status recomputed from disk; goal/root read from the journal (the evaluator's own task spec)" would be improvements, not defect fixes.

Out of scope of this claim, noted only for the parent: results/p4-hp/p4_tests.txt (UTF-16) records an older crash-test version failing (1 failed, 27 passed) while DECISIONS.md:40 states 28/28 "with modified test code" — the matching log is not in results/. Also supervisor.py:121-122 creates the workspace dir (mkdir exist_ok=False) before begin_episode; a kill in that window would make every restart raise FileExistsError until max_restarts. Neither affects the refutation above.

The factual observations hold (same predicate at supervisor.py:90-91,97 and supervise.py:71-73; both observe() read disk fresh, fs_world.py:99-100 / view_world.py:63-65; the dup metric on the TEXT PRIMARY KEY, journal.py:17, is tautologically 0) but the defect inference does not. (1) Not 'by construction': verify_from_disk ignores status/result.completed and re-derives the verdict from disk; on a scratch copy of runs/p4_crash_local, deleting one must-file of a done episode produced really_done 39 / false_done ['sup-0'], i.e. the check would catch the supervisor-side faults P4 targets (done-from-belief, acting on a root other than the recorded one, ws diverging from disk) - none are 'external writers'. (2) The 'weakened/wrong goal' case is unreachable: the goal originates from the evaluator's own generator (supervise.py:30-36 -> BODIES make_task) and is persisted verbatim at supervisor.py:122; applying the proposed remedy retroactively (regenerating all 40 goals via eval/generator.make_task from meta.index/split, which meta already carries, generator.py:80) gives 40/40 identical to the journal's goals, so the recorded result does not depend on this; generation is seeded only by (split,index) so HP is identical by construction. (3) The duplicate invariant is enforced and a violation would fail the crash test: journal.intent (loop.py:63) is outside the try/except, the IntegrityError (confirmed: 'UNIQUE constraint failed: actions.id') propagates through run_supervisor so summary.json (supervise.py:56) is never written and crash_test ends with final=None -> ok=False (supervise.py:137-142); '중복 0' is true, the metric merely redundant (LOW nit). (4) DECISIONS.md:37 describes exactly what the code does; P2_P4_REPORT.md:81's 'did not trust the journal' refers to the completion claim and §5.6 is labelled non-pre-registered engineering verification (:74). No reachable case yields a wrong verify result and no recorded number changes; residual is a wording/redundant-metric nit, not MED.

findings.title: crash_test reports ok=True without requiring any kill, let alone a kill inside the intent->act->verify window; pace_s sleep adds kill-safe time
findings.claim: The headline `ok` printed by `python -m atanor_os crash` is true whenever the final journal is consistent; it does not depend on kills >= 1 nor on any action having been reconciled (i.e. on a kill ever landing between journal.intent() and journal.mark('verified')). The new pace_s parameter makes the supervisor sleep between episodes, i.e. adds time in which a kill tests nothing, and test_process_level_crash_test passes pace_s=0.25 and only asserts kills >= 1. The deterministic unit test covers only the 'intended'-after-execute path; the 'executed' status, the 'not_done' (kill before execute) path and the 'unknown' path are untested, so the recorded 3 window hits (2 machines) are the only evidence and they are incidental.

findings.title: A timing-dependent process-level crash test is inside the pre-registration validity gate (-k 'not learning'), so a flake spuriously INVALIDATEs a frozen run
findings.claim: cmd_pilot computes checks['tests_passed'] = run_tests(out, 'not learning'); the selection now collects test_process_level_crash_test, which spawns subprocesses and kills them at wall-clock delays. Its outcome depends on machine speed/load and on the restart wedge above, so a pre-registered scientific run (protocol invalid_if: 'validity tests not run or failed') can be judged INVALID because an engineering test flaked -- the same failure mode that already cost results/p1-test-03-scarce. The gate also includes the 'kills >= 1' assertion which is purely timing-based.
findings.evidence: run.py:269: `'tests_passed': None if a.skip_tests else run_tests(out, 'not learning')`; run.py:209: `[sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', str(PKG / 'tests'), '-q', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider', '-k', expr]`. pytest --collect-only -k 'not learning' lists `tests/test_supervisor.py::test_process_level_crash_test` (25/28 collected). metrics.py:87-88: `ck.get('tests_passed') is not True` -> INVALID. results/p2-h2-01/tests_not_learning.txt and results/p3-view-01/tests_not_learning.txt: '22 passed, 3 deselected' (the gate did include it).
findings.remedy: Exclude process-level / timing tests from the validity gate (e.g. name them *_process_* and use -k 'not learning and not process', or a pytest marker), keeping the deterministic SimulatedCrash tests; run the engineering tests separately and record them in checks under their own key.

votes.reason:

The first spawn is therefore always killed; the assertion cannot fail by timing on any machine.

2. "Outcome depends on machine speed/load" describes the previous version of the test, not this one. results/p4-hp/p4_tests.txt shows that older test (n_episodes=15, max_restarts=80, no pace, fixed window) failing on the slow HP with restarts 80 / kills 80 / natural_exits 0 and the kill_delays never growing. The current crash_test grows the window by 1.5x on every kill that finished no episode (supervise.py:132-134, progress = journal.count_episodes() of done/failed rows, journal.py:81-84), so no-progress kills are logarithmically bounded and progress kills are bounded by n_episodes=10; 120 restarts cannot be exhausted by slowness, only by a genuine supervisor defect, which is what the test exists to catch (a true positive, not a flake). DECISIONS.md line 40 records the fixed test passing 28/28 on HP; locally it passed 3/3 consecutive runs in ~5.2 s each. The only timing path to a spurious failure I could construct is the kill landing in the microseconds between creation and write of summary.json (supervise.py:56 -> json.loads of an empty file at :116); that is a negligible-probability LOW hardening item, not a MED gate defect.

3. "(the gate did include it)" for results/p2-h2-01 and results/p3-view-01 is false: their tests_not_learning.txt say "22 passed, 3 deselected" = 25 tests collected, written 09:43, whereas tests/test_supervisor.py (the 3 P4 tests that bring the total to 28) is dated 09:57. The protocol text makes this a documented rule, not a deviation: EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md:51 defines INVALID as "validity tests (excluding learner performance tests) not run or failed", which is exactly `-k 'not learning'` at run.py:269-270; all three frozen protocols say "validity tests not run or failed". Whether a process-level P4 test should count as a validity test is a design preference about gate scope, not a defect that can be pointed to in code or protocol.

5. The analogy to results/p1-test-03-scarce does not support a flake risk: DECISIONS.md line 32 attributes that INVALID to three deterministic test_view failures caused by developing P3 code in the same tree during the run (the recorded tests_not_learning.txt shows the assertion mismatches), already remediated by snapshot runs and the source_changed_during_run check (run.py:257, 287-288).

A kill landing between the mkdir and the begin_episode commit leaves ws/ep{idx} on disk with no episode row; on every restart supervisor.py:119 `idx = self.journal.count_episodes(any_status=True)` yields the same idx, make_task raises FileExistsError and the process exits 1 in ~0.19 s (reproduced by pre-creating ws/ep0 and running `python -m atanor_os supervise`). These are natural exits, so the adaptive window in eval/supervise.py:132-134 (`if adaptive and _finished(root) == before` is only evaluated in the TimeoutExpired/kill branch) never widens, and 117 natural exits exhaust max_restarts=120. The failed run's pytest tmp root confirms it: ws/ep0..ep5 exist, episodes table holds sup-0..sup-4 all 'done', none running, no summary.json. (3) The scarce INVALID (DECISIONS.md:32) was a deterministic failure of concurrently edited test_view.py, not a flake; only the consequence (engineering test -> INVALID) is the same.

Side note for the parent: the same evidence shows a genuine P4 defect (workspace creation is not idempotent across a kill in that gap), which contradicts the "survives a kill at any moment" claim in DECISIONS.md:37 / P2_P4_REPORT.md:14 and is a separate finding.

Reproduction (same code, seed=2, machine ANSEOK-9950X3D): 11 runs of the test -> 9 passed (~5 s), 2 FAILED (23.3 s and 23.05 s). Failing crash_log: {"restarts":120,"kills":3,"natural_exits":117,"no_progress_kills":0,"final_summary":null,"verify":{"episodes":5,"running":0,"unresolved_actions":0,...},"ok":false} — after the third kill every restart died at startup. The "already handled" defence fails: the adaptive window (supervise.py:132-134) only reacts to kills.

Corrections to the claim's evidence (do not change the verdict): (1) `kills >= 1` is not timing-flaky — pace_s=0.25 x 10 episodes >= 2.5 s of sleep vs a <=0.9 s first delay, so the first spawn is always killed (kills=3 even in the failing run). (2) The cited recorded gates did NOT include this test: p2-h2-01 and p3-view-01 ran their gates 09:43:36-41 from snapshot snap_atanor_0945 (computed sha 6ac1457be2fcf22c = DECISIONS line 41), which has no test_supervisor.py (created 09:50:27); "22 passed, 3 deselected" = 25 collected = the suite minus the three supervisor tests. (3) p1-test-03-scarce was invalidated by three deterministic test_view.py failures from concurrent edits (its tests_not_learning.txt), not a timing flake. (4) The machine-speed path (results/p4-hp/p4_tests.txt, old test n=15/max_restarts=80, 80 kills, 0 natural exits) was already fixed at 09:57 by the adaptive window + pace_s; the residual nondeterminism is kill-moment-dependent, not speed-dependent.

Consequence: a future pre-registered P1-P3 pilot, whose code path never touches Supervisor, is judged INVALID with roughly 10-20% probability per run because of a P4 restart wedge — wrong behaviour in a reachable case (MED; conservative, never a false VALID). Note the failure is a TRUE positive for P4, so the proposed remedy (drop process tests from the gate) would hide a real defect; the fix is idempotent episode setup (journal the episode before creating its workspace, or tolerate/clean an existing ws/epN on restart), and the DECISIONS lines 37-40 claim "built to be killed at any moment and restarted" is itself overclaimed.

findings.title: rule_agreement's 'exact/learned' label is over-generous: failure cells are dominated by type-mismatch failures, predicted 'unknown' effects never count as errors, and exact is computed even when cells are unfilled
findings.claim: Stratification is only by (tool, true outcome). The failure cell of a 2-ary tool is sampled uniformly over all syntactically valid failing actions, which are overwhelmingly type mismatches (e.g. group(ext:txt, p1), copy(dir, file)); the subtle precondition failures the learner is known to over-generalize on (DECISIONS.md:35 '일부는 대조 부족으로 과일반', e.g. group on a filtered panel, copy into an absent parent) are ~1 of ~200 failing actions per state, so with k=20 a tool whose rule misses that literal is still labelled exact with high probability. eff is counted only when the model commits to a value (predicted 'unknown' matches anything), so a rule whose effects collapsed to 'unknown' is 'exact'. exact_tools/n_exact are computed regardless of `filled`, and the REPORT table omits `filled`. The H3 transfer criterion ('C has >= 5 of 6 tools learned in >= 4 of 5 seeds') is defined on this label. Sampling itself is model-independent (same rng path for every condition within a seed), so pairing across conditions is sound; the bias is in what the label certifies, and it is train-distribution only as the protocol declares.
findings.evidence: oracle.py:135-142: `for tool, args in ws.actions(sorted(pre)): outcome = 'success' if pre_fn(pre, tool, args) else 'failure'; buckets.setdefault(f'{tool}:{outcome}', []).append((tool, args))` ... `cell = rng.choice(needy); tool, args = rng.choice(buckets[cell])`. oracle.py:154-156: `elif res['ok'] and not all(predicted[a][k_] in ('unknown', post[a].get(k_)) ...): pt['eff'] += 1`. oracle.py:158: `exact = sorted(t for t, v in per_tool.items() if v['checks'] and v['fp'] == v['fn'] == v['eff'] == 0)` (no `filled` condition). metrics.py:135-136 builds the report row without `filled`. protocol_view.json:14: 'A tool counts as learned when fp = fn = eff = 0. Transfer claim for the body: C has >= 5 of 6 tools learned in >= 4 of 5 seeds'.
findings.remedy: Stratify failures further by lifted signature or by which true-precondition literal is violated (>= k per violated literal), or oversample near-miss failures (one literal from a success); add an 'unknown' counter (predicted attributes left unknown on real successes) and require filled=True for the learned label; print filled and unknown in the report table. Since protocol_view.json is frozen, record this as a known limit of the secondary measure rather than changing the criterion after results.

findings.title: Planner charges a two-primitive macro one depth unit, giving E a deeper effective horizon than CT
